summary:
plan.md is written. It describes a symmetrical, two-storey red-brick hall (33 × 17) on a grey stone plinth, with a slate civic hip roof, pavilions at the front corners and white quartz dressings. A four-column portico with a pediment carries the words TOWN HALL. A clock tower with a copper spire rises behind the portico and reads as civic from a distance. No roof dry-run or render was made. Symmetrical Victorian-Georgian brick town hall: quartz four-column portico with oculus pediment, slate hip roof, clock tower with copper spire, twin chimneys with lit campfires.
Ground: vestibule, hall with twin grand stairs, bays, two offices with fireplaces; upper: council chamber, two committee rooms, clock room, belfry.
Six parts by trade: shell, roofs, dressings, fittings/lettering, chimneys, grounds.

concept_subject: A Victorian market-town hall on a flat green lot facing north onto a paved street. The main body is a symmetrical two-storey block of warm red brick, 33 wide and 17 deep. It stands on a raised grey andesite plinth with a stone water table. A white quartz string course marks the first floor and a white quartz dentil cornice runs under the eaves. White quartz quoins stand at every corner, and two end pavilions step one block forward at the front corners. Above is a grey slate hip roof with a stone ridge, small gable dormers and two brick chimneys, one near each end, each with a dark band, a slab cap and a curl of smoke. At the centre of the front, a broad stair of stone steps climbs to a portico of four white quartz columns. They carry a white entablature lettered TOWN HALL in dark letters, under a slate-roofed triangular pediment with a white tympanum and a round oculus. Behind it are a dark oak front door with glass sidelights and a fanlight, and a three-light Palladian window above. Rising from the roof just behind the pediment is a square red-brick clock tower with white quoins. It has a white clock face with black hands on each side, an open belfry with a bronze bell, and a white cornice, and it is crowned by a steep verdigris-green copper pyramid spire with a lightning-rod finial. Every window is tall and glazed, with white quartz sills, keystone flat arches below and hood moulds above. In front, lawns sit either side of the steps, with a flagpole flying a blue banner on each lawn and lantern posts flanking the stair. Behind the hall a gravel path runs through a rear garden between two oaks.
